bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation after PCI, dual therapy with dabigatran 110 mg plus a P2Y12 inhibitor had a lower incidence of major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than triple therapy with warfarin (15.4% vs. 26.9%; hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42 to 0.63).
implications: These data support the conclusion that, in this trial population, dabigatran-based dual therapy lowered ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus warfarin-based triple therapy (e.g., 15.4% vs. 26.9%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.63 for the 110-mg comparison; 20.2% vs. 25.7%; HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.88 for the 150-mg comparison) while the combined dual-therapy groups were noninferior to triple therapy for the composite efficacy end point (13.7% vs. 13.4%; HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.29). The results do not establish comparative effects on individual efficacy components because the trial notes it was not powered for those comparisons and some component differences were nonsignificant.

major_points.text: Multicenter randomized trial in AF patients after PCI comparing dabigatran-based dual therapy vs warfarin-based triple therapy including aspirin for 1–3 months.
major_points.quote: In this multicenter trial, we randomly assigned 2725 patients with atrial fibrillation who had undergone PCI to triple therapy with warfarin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor (clopidogrel or ticagrelor) and aspirin (for 1 to 3 months) ... or dual therapy with dabigatran

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding over follow-up (mean 14 months).
major_points.quote: The primary end point was a major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding event during follow-up (mean follow-up, 14 months).

major_points.text: 110-mg dabigatran dual therapy reduced bleeding versus triple therapy and met both noninferiority and superiority for the primary endpoint.
major_points.quote: 15.4% in the 110-mg dual-therapy group as compared with 26.9% in the triple-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.63; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P<0.001 for superiority)

major_points.text: 150-mg dabigatran dual therapy reduced bleeding versus its corresponding triple-therapy group and was noninferior for the primary endpoint.
major_points.quote: 20.2% in the 150-mg dual-therapy group as compared with 25.7% in the corresponding triple-therapy group ... (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.88; P<0.001 for noninferiority)

major_points.text: Composite efficacy endpoint (thromboembolic events, death, or unplanned revascularization) was noninferior for combined dual-therapy groups vs triple therapy.
major_points.quote: The incidence of the composite efficacy end point was 13.7% in the two dual-therapy groups combined as compared with 13.4% in the triple-therapy group (hazard ratio, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.29; P = 0.005 for noninferiority).

major_points.text: Open-label design with blinded independent adjudication of end points.
major_points.quote: The trial had an open-label design; however, all primary and secondary end-point events were adjudicated by an independent committee whose members were unaware of the treatment assignments.

criticisms.text: Protocol amended to enroll fewer patients than originally planned, limiting power to examine efficacy according to dabigatran dose.
criticisms.quote: we amended the protocol and enrolled a smaller num- ber of patients than we had originally planned to enroll, and this limits the power of the trial to examine efficacy according to dabigatran dose.

criticisms.text: Cannot determine relative contributions of aspirin omission vs type of oral anticoagulant; only speculation possible without factorial design.
criticisms.quote: we may only speculate on the relative contributions of the omission of aspirin and the type of oral antico- agulant in the dual-therapy groups and the tri- ple-therapy group.

criticisms.text: Trial was not powered to compare individual components of the composite efficacy endpoint; caution needed interpreting small nonsignificant numerical excesses.
